Manufacturer accessory and proposed reaction saddle — digital study

The Orbitform HL-200 manufacturer page links an accessory STEP and one-page inch drawing. Original PDF/STEP bytes, retrieval metadata and hashes are retained in heading-accessory-source/manifest.json; the earlier custody originals remain under history/. The source is an attachment, not a complete machine. It gives no custom peen/contact geometry or dimensioned opposing fixture for this hinge.

Source registration and dimensions

Mainline maps the housing's native cylindrical axis and the distal blank's terminal plane. The study origin is their intersection; local +X runs outward toward the housing, +Z is up. No native geometry is rescaled. Eight valid solids are retained with source labels rather than assigning unverified manufacturer component roles.

Its general tolerances are document information, not certified as-made tool tolerances.

Declared placement and motion

The main-axis intersection with the blank terminal plane is placed0.5 mm outward from each saved final pin-head face. This is a geometric standoff, not a heading contact or forming stroke. The nearest tilted rim remains about0.2231 mm outward in this nominal placement. Saved gates are closed and both already-formed heads remain present; no rod upset, material flow or initial-head sequence is simulated.

The manufacturer describes an angled peen on a rotating spindle, and its Assembly Solutions Guide, printed p.2/PDF p.4, illustrates angle, stroke and peen. Printed p.12/PDF p.14 distinguishes an anti-rotate device from orbital motion. Neither source maps the eight native STEP solids to actual joints. Consequently this study evaluates declared rigid clocking of the entire saved accessory, not real internal orbital kinematics.

A continuous upper envelope is constructed for those declared rigid orientations. Axial partitions include each source solid's bounds and maximum8 mm intervals. Their radial bounds use enclosing circles, a checked global housing-radius cylinder, and an analytic oblique-cylinder bound where only the verified distal blank occurs. The slices are fused to one valid solid; source containment is tested at independent clock angles. A clear envelope establishes clearance for the declared rigid rotations within kernel tolerance. An envelope intersection alone does not establish a native collision; native30° samples are used where necessary, or the case remains unresolved. Fixture geometry is checked first. If it already intersects an obstacle, the combined setup is blocked and accessory-envelope/pose checks are explicitly skipped; otherwise the envelope is checked, with native sampling only where needed.

These tests do not evaluate a continuous axial insertion path. The prior312 cylindrical approaches retain their separate scope. Powerhead, operator, clamps, custom contact tool and unverified internal motion are omitted.

Proposed support geometry

A three-piece reaction-saddle concept sits outside the pan for early hinge assembly: an anvil-side L-block, a forming-side L-block and a separate base. Their dimensions are shared design assumptions in P5_HEADING_STUDY, not manufacturer fixture dimensions. Each block is25 ×18 ×18 mm at its upper pad, with a4 mm post setback; the base is6 mm thick. The forming side has a12 mm clearance bore/slot. The anvil pocket is6.4 mm diameter and1.5 mm deep, derived from the nominal6 ×1.2 mm final head and half the0.6 mm axial float.

The pads nominally touch the fixed-cheek outer faces; the anvil pocket bottom touches the saved opposite head. These are geometry contacts, not proven forming-load paths. Fixture pieces may be positioned/removed independently; fastening/clamping and force capacity are unresolved. The base is below the gate. Saved moving hardware is checked at0–60° in10° steps; this is not a continuous motion, hot-clearance or post-heading float result.

The manufacturer's pivot-fixture example motivates supporting fixed parts without pinching the moving joint. Powerhead sizing guidance says stainless requires more force than mild steel; capacity comparisons do not qualify this pin. No production tooling or stainless capability is adopted.

Decision boundary

The generated assessment reports all26 pin ends in four assembly stages. Proposed-fixture collisions are concrete contradictions for that geometry and stage, not proof that every fixture or process fails. The next design decisions are actual custom-contact geometry, machine/powerhead envelope, clamping and joining access, and a source-supported initial-head/retention route. Pin grade/hardness, forming force, distortion and physical retention remain outside the digital result. No physical fit measurement is required to continue this project.
